papers.title: Learning Robot Metareasoning: Adaptive Computation Budgets for Real-Time Control
papers.abstract: Planning while moving faces an historical trade-off between deliberation and reactivity. A planner running concurrently with execution needs time to compute, so the robot must commit to an open-loop action chunk for that duration: a longer commitment buys a better plan at the cost of feedback frequency. Existing controllers fix this action commitment, and consequently the computation budget, before deployment. However, the optimal computation time is highly state-dependent (due to factors such as unmodeled dynamics, safety constraints, and marginal optimisation gains), i.e. dynamic, therefore offline static tuning risks leaving systems blind during critical maneuvers or unable to find global effective solutions. We cast the identification of the optimal computation budget as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) in which a single decision defines both the robot action commitments and the time allocated to the solver. To solve this, we train a reinforcement-learning policy conditioned on the current state, the executing plan, and inexpensive planner statistics. Across ground-robot navigation, agile quadrotor flight, and contact-rich manipulation, the learned policy changes its budget with the demands of the scenario, discovering efficient reasoning patterns that outperform fixed-budget baselines. https://lorenzomagnino.github.io/learning-robot-metareasoning-review/
papers.overview_sentence: Planning while moving faces an historical trade-off between deliberation and reactivity.

repos.description: A Tiny biped duck robot 🦆. Contribute to pollen-robotics/microduck development by creating an account on GitHub.
repos.readme_excerpt: Microduck A tiny biped robot that moves using reinforcement learning policies. Get yours here · Cheat sheet · Training the policies · How it works · Contributing This repo is the duck's brain. About 25 cm and 800 g of robot, run by a handful of daemons on a Rockchip RK3566: a 50 Hz control loop driving fifteen servos from neural policies, the radios and the camera, and the update machinery that gets new software onto a robot without bricking it. Everything you need to run a Microduck is here. If you want one, get yours here . The policies it runs are trained next door, in microduck_rl — MuJoCo and PPO, the sim2real recipe, and the export to ONNX that this repo loads. It does things walk.MP4 roller_cut.mp4 It walks. Pick up a gamepad and drive. It rolls. Put wheels on, ask for roller mode, and it loads the other brain. grasp.MP4 standup.MP4 It picks things up. Beak to the floor, one button. It gets back up. Knock it over and it stands itself up. It also sits, kicks a ball, rolls forward on command, and quacks in a voice that is its own. Where to find things You have a duck Cheat sheet Every robotctl command: drive, configure, voice, chorale, theremin, wifi, updates, logs. Start her…

repos.readme_excerpt: ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics Project Page | Paper ASPIRE is a new type of continual learning: "training" is skill refinement instead of gradient descent.
